evals.name: catalogue-no-arguments
evals.prompt: Use oneshot-websites.
evals.expected_output: Makes the complete current prompt catalogue the first substantive response content, grouped by namespace with a one-line namespace explanation and one-line description for every prompt, then invites a selection or custom brief.

assertions.text: Runs and presents the unfiltered catalogue before asking a question or presenting any other choice
Shows all namespaces and every prompt as an ID-and-slug option with a one-line explanation
Does not make catalogue listing a later option or expect the user to know an unseen slug
Does not invent a website brief or pick a template for the user

evals.name: contextual-baselines
evals.prompt: I want to explore ideas for an interactive public-transit experience, but I have not settled on a direction yet.
evals.expected_output: Searches the catalogue and offers the closest optional baselines while keeping an original user brief equally available.

assertions.text: Uses catalogue search rather than declaring a single mandatory template
Makes clear that the suggestions are optional

evals.name: direct-refined-dispatch
evals.prompt: Build a calm, tactile museum guide for a small collection of kinetic sculptures. Keep the first sentence exactly as written.
evals.expected_output: Produces a faithful actual prompt of no more than two paragraphs, preserves the explicitly protected first sentence exactly, writes the refined prompt's exact UTF-8 bytes to artifact/PROMPT.md, anchors its SHA-256 digest in a coordinator-owned pre-dispatch receipt, and includes the same refined text in the fresh lead's initial dispatch.

assertions.text: Preserves the protected first sentence while refining the remaining brief into no more than two paragraphs
Anchors the refined actual prompt's exact bytes outside the worker-owned run
Does not replace the user brief with a framework or template recipe
The fresh lead dispatch and artifact/PROMPT.md contain the same refined actual prompt

evals.name: fresh-leads-for-multiple-briefs
evals.prompt: Make two independent experiences: a storm-chasing field notebook and a playful reef survey. Compare Model A and Model B in Harness X.
evals.expected_output: Reserves one collision-free model/harness/experiment/run namespace for every requested matrix cell and dispatches one distinct fresh lead for each artifact.

assertions.text: Does not combine multiple artifacts into one worker
Keeps model, harness, experiment, and run identity in that order
Creates exactly four isolated runs owned by four distinct fresh leads for the two briefs across two models

evals.name: recursive-delegation-without-budgets
evals.prompt: Create an ambitious illustrated weather laboratory. Use any collaborators you need and keep improving it until the result is ready.
evals.expected_output: Lets the owning lead choose its tools, stack, workflow, iteration, and recursive subagents. It imposes no time, token, step, tool-call, dependency, source-file, or goal-mode limits.

assertions.text: Permits recursive delegation inside the assigned run
Does not add arbitrary budgets or require goal mode

evals.name: framework-to-static-artifact
evals.prompt: Create a multi-view launch explorer with rich transitions and a responsive route map.
evals.expected_output: Allows the lead to use a framework project in workspace/ and requires its production export in artifact/, with artifact/PROMPT.md and a root artifact/index.html that can be deployed without installation, build, or an application server.

assertions.text: Does not reject a chosen framework project
Checks the final static handoff rather than a source-file shape

evals.name: collision-free-identities
evals.prompt: Run the same harbour experience under model names 'Model One' and 'Model-One'.
evals.expected_output: Derives readable identity keys with exact-name digests, produces distinct paths for the two normalized-similar names, and creates a new run ID for every execution.

assertions.text: Never overwrites an existing run
Records raw names and derived keys in run.json

evals.name: unsupported-no-subagent-harness
evals.prompt: The current harness cannot create any fresh subagents. Please generate the site yourself as a stand-in.
evals.expected_output: Stops before artifact generation and reports UNSUPPORTED_NO_FRESH_SUBAGENT. It does not imitate isolation with the coordinator or reuse a same-context worker.

assertions.text: Treats fresh-subagent support as a hard dependency
Does not substitute coordinator generation
Reports the exact UNSUPPORTED_NO_FRESH_SUBAGENT status

evals.name: catalogue-extension
evals.prompt: Add a new prompt template for a hands-on river restoration planning experience.
evals.expected_output: Reads the catalogue authoring rules, appends a unique stable ID, slug, title, category, prompt, and lowercase tags, and leaves existing entries unchanged and implementation-open.

assertions.text: Does not renumber or reuse existing prompt IDs
Avoids prescribing a framework, library, version, or single-file recipe

evals.name: artifact-validation
evals.prompt: Explain the oneshot-websites validation workflow you would apply before publishing an output root. Assume one successful run was built from a framework workspace and exported as static files.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the catalogue validator and explains that it checks namespace, the independent prompt receipt, status evidence, fixed local paths, Drop bounds, and artifact/index.html. It accepts the framework workspace and would report any missing successful entrypoint or unsafe final artifact.

assertions.text: Identifies artifact/PROMPT.md and artifact/index.html as validation targets
Does not impose a vanilla or single-file implementation rule

evals.name: custom-brief-without-catalogue-match
evals.prompt: Create a private one-shot memorial for a fictional lighthouse keeper. The interaction must follow my exact seven-scene oral-history sequence, use only the supplied family vocabulary, and preserve my scene wording unchanged. Do not turn it into a game, dashboard, or generic maritime story.
evals.expected_output: Refines the custom brief into at most two paragraphs while preserving the seven-scene sequence, family-vocabulary boundary, exact scene wording, and non-game intent. It does not splice in catalogue ideas, and the refined text becomes both the lead dispatch and artifact/PROMPT.md.

assertions.text: Produces a faithful one- or two-paragraph refinement that preserves every explicit constraint and exact wording requirement
Does not force a weak catalogue match or hybridize the brief
Stores and dispatches the same refined actual prompt

evals.name: custom-brief-with-relevant-catalogue-match
evals.prompt: Create a browser-based submarine command simulator with sonar, ballast controls, instrument failures, abyssal navigation, and a crew whose survival depends on my mission sequence.
evals.expected_output: May offer the materially relevant Submarine Command Game catalogue item as an optional baseline. Until the user accepts it, the custom route remains a faithful one- or two-paragraph refinement containing only the user's simulator goal and loose guidance derived from it.

assertions.text: Offers a genuinely relevant catalogue match as optional rather than mandatory
Does not splice catalogue language into the custom brief without acceptance
Uses the refined custom prompt for dispatch and PROMPT.md unless the user accepts the baseline

evals.name: no-history-lead-isolation
evals.prompt: Run this one-shot in Codex, where spawned agents inherit the current conversation unless configured otherwise.
evals.expected_output: Creates the owning lead with spawn_agent fork_turns set to none, then explicitly includes the lead role, exact actual prompt, assigned run path, and experiment metadata in that empty-history dispatch.

assertions.text: Uses fork_turns none instead of the history-inheriting spawn default
Does not leak coordinator or sibling conversation into the lead context
Still passes the actual prompt text and lead role explicitly

evals.name: undecided-user-does-not-know-slugs
evals.prompt: Use oneshot-websites. Allow me to choose, but I don't know the prompt IDs or slugs yet.
evals.expected_output: Immediately shows the complete unfiltered catalogue grouped by namespace, with a one-line explanation for every namespace and prompt. It does not defer, ask for an unknown slug, or merely explain how to request the list.

assertions.text: The first substantive response content is the complete namespace-grouped catalogue
Every option includes both its stable ID and slug plus a one-line explanation
Does not reply with instructions to send a slug later

evals.name: rough-unmatched-custom-brief
evals.prompt: Windows XP clone on a web interface
evals.expected_output: Refines the fragment into a vivid actual prompt of no more than two paragraphs. The result keeps the Windows XP web-clone goal, adds loose guidance for an explorable desktop with tactile windows, familiar system surfaces, responsive motion, and playful discoveries, avoids unrelated catalogue material and stack prescriptions, and becomes the exact prompt stored in artifact/PROMPT.md and sent to the lead.

assertions.text: Turns the fragment into a clear one- or two-paragraph experience brief rather than dispatching it unchanged
Adds only loose interaction, atmosphere, and motion guidance consistent with a Windows XP web interface
Does not inject a catalogue premise or require Three.js, React, or another implementation choice
The refined text is exactly the prompt sent to the lead and preserved in artifact/PROMPT.md

evals.name: catalogue-entry-inherits-interactive-direction
evals.prompt: Use ow-075, Forest Fungi Explorer, as the one-shot prompt.
evals.expected_output: Uses the ow-075 goal as source material and crafts a cohesive one- or two-paragraph actual prompt with forest-specific interaction, motion, spatial or ambient behavior, and concise integrated text. The shared experienceDirection guides composition silently and is absent from the lead dispatch and artifact/PROMPT.md.

assertions.text: Preserves the selected catalogue goal while turning the shared posture into concrete forest-specific possibilities
Does not copy, label, or mechanically paraphrase the catalogue experienceDirection in the actual prompt
Does not prescribe Three.js or any other framework, library, or version
The same finished actual prompt is dispatched and preserved in artifact/PROMPT.md

evals.name: text-critical-format-keeps-copy
evals.prompt: Create a public-health CMS and campaign landing page where editors publish long-form guidance, FAQs, service updates, and translated resources.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the content-heavy CMS and landing-page purpose intact. It can still encourage polished interaction and motion where useful, but it does not suppress, trivialize, or replace the long-form and operational text the requested format needs.

assertions.text: Treats the requested long-form guidance and CMS content as core product material
Does not apply the concise-text default as a ban on necessary copy

evals.name: root-entrypoint-allows-rich-asset-tree
evals.prompt: Create an explorable miniature planet with animated weather, spatial audio, custom illustrations, and several interactive regions.
evals.expected_output: Requires one exact root artifact/index.html entrypoint while allowing the production artifact to include all built scripts, styles, audio, images, fonts, models, shaders, data, and asset directories needed for the strongest drop-ready experience.

assertions.text: Keeps artifact/index.html as the single root entrypoint
Allows and encourages a multi-file artifact with supporting asset directories
Does not collapse the result into one HTML file merely to satisfy the entrypoint rule

evals.name: accepted-baseline-context-keeps-shared-direction
evals.prompt: Use ow-092, Submarine Command Game, as the baseline and add my context: the crew is mapping a newly opened trench for a live science broadcast.
evals.expected_output: After baseline acceptance, crafts a cohesive one- or two-paragraph actual prompt that preserves the ow-092 goal and the live-broadcast trench context. It silently applies any relevant interactive direction without including the shared experienceDirection or internal provenance labels. The fresh lead and artifact/PROMPT.md receive the finished prompt unchanged.

assertions.text: Preserves the accepted catalogue goal and every explicit user addition in a cohesive finished brief
Does not include an EXPERIENCE DIRECTION block, the literal shared direction, or internal provenance labels
Does not splice unrelated catalogue content into the user context
Dispatch and artifact/PROMPT.md contain the same finished actual prompt

evals.name: catalogue-guidance-never-leaks-into-prompt
evals.prompt: Use ow-083, Floating Island Atlas, as the one-shot prompt.
evals.expected_output: Crafts a specific one- or two-paragraph floating-archipelago brief from the catalogue goal, using the internal visual and interaction posture to suggest native possibilities such as charting routes through drifting weather and discovering changing islands. The generic experienceDirection is not copied or exposed in the lead dispatch or artifact/PROMPT.md.

assertions.text: The actual prompt remains specifically about the drifting archipelago, its weather, routes, cultures, ecosystems, and encounters
artifact/PROMPT.md does not contain the sentence beginning 'Default to a visually led, interaction-first experience'
The lead dispatch does not contain a labelled EXPERIENCE DIRECTION block or generic coordinator guidance
The same finished actual prompt is dispatched and stored in artifact/PROMPT.md

evals.name: catalogue-labels-are-plain-and-scan-friendly
evals.prompt: Use oneshot-websites without arguments. I am in a hurry and need to scan all 100 choices quickly.
evals.expected_output: Lists the complete catalogue by namespace using short literal titles and plain one-line descriptions, while keeping richer source prompts out of the browsing menu. A first-person shooter is labelled First-Person Shooter Game rather than with a fictional or lore-like title.

assertions.text: Every prompt option has a short literal title and a plain one-line description
The ow-093 option is titled First-Person Shooter Game
The browsing list uses prompt descriptions rather than dumping the richer source prompt text
Does not replace clear format names with lore, coined brands, or mood-only labels
